overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated recent uploads reveals extreme outperformance in space curiosity-gap scenarios, specifically 'What If' planetary exploration formats combined with high-value descriptors (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, dark planets, extreme rain phenomena). Videos published within the last 7 days targeting bizarre planetary conditions achieve the highest velocity, views-per-day, and engagement rates (likes-per-view). General biology and psychological trivia from earlier weeks show much lower engagement velocity, indicating audience preference has heavily pivoted toward cinematic, high-stakes astronomical hypotheticals.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 972 views rapidly with strong like counts (38 and 18 respectively), massively outperforming standard static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If You Fell Into...' scenarios focusing on extreme, visually striking exoplanets.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme materials such as 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies! 💎' (QXuqYERlqSo) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b 🌌' (v1rrcZLdp4U) drove over 700 to 1,026 views with exceptionally high engagement ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing high-impact superlatives ('darker than coal', 'supersonic', 'liquid metal') applied to cosmic bodies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, 5 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc, 71 views) show flatlining velocity and poor engagement compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia and song-stuck hooks for upcoming shorts.

weak_patterns.pattern: Standard Animal Fact Lists without Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) yield moderate views initially but flatline quickly with zero comments and minimal likes.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from static listicles toward cinematic survival or high-stakes evolutionary anomalies.

next_video.concept: Surviving on a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with no star.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with total pitch blackness and absolute sub-zero temperature, asking the viewer what happens when a world is ejected from its solar system.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite having no sun, volcanoes powered by crushing tidal forces create glowing lakes of liquid nitrogen that could theoretically harbor alien ecosystems.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary exploration format while introducing a fresh cosmic phenomenon (rogue planets and nitrogen lakes) distinct from previous diamond/ice planet topics.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not mention diamond planets, liquid metal rain, or Saturn's rings.
Focus exclusively on rogue interstellar bodies.
Maintain scientific accuracy regarding tidal heating.

experiment: Test a 21-second narrative pacing structure with an instant zero-second visual hook (pitch black screen transitioning to a glowing alien world) to measure retention impact against standard 16-19 second formatting.
